australia/riverina.text: A large irrigated region in the Big Rivers zone of New South Wales, centered on Griffith and relying heavily on the Murrumbidgee Irrigation Scheme. It makes 60% of the state's grapes and 25% of Australian wine. Syrah and Chardonnay lead the plantings.

australia/riverland.text: An irrigated region of river flats along the Murray River in South Australia, and the only region in the Lower Murray zone. It has about 53,900 acres of vines. Syrah is the most planted grape, followed by Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon.

australia/robe.text: A small South Australian region in the Limestone Coast zone, next to the town of Robe. It became an Australian Geographical Indication in 2006.

australia/rutherglen.text: A North East Victoria region around the town of Rutherglen, particularly noted for its sweet fortified wines. Plantings are led by Syrah, followed by Petite Sirah and Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains.

australia/shoalhaven-coast.text: A New South Wales region in the South Coast zone, with only about 100 acres of vines.

australia/south-australia.text: The state that makes about half of all Australian wine. Its range runs from Riesling in Clare Valley to big, full-bodied Shiraz in Barossa Valley, and it is home to Penfolds Grange and Jacob's Creek. Irrigation is vital here.

australia/south-coast.text: A New South Wales zone containing Shoalhaven Coast and Southern Highlands, with about 740 acres of vines over a large area. Chardonnay is the most planted grape, followed by Merlot and Syrah.

australia/south-eastern-australia.text: A broad zone in south-eastern Australia, listed directly under the country rather than under a state. It works as a wide geographic label, not a single style of wine.

australia/south-west-australia.text: A large Western Australia zone containing Margaret River, Great Southern, Geographe, Manjimup, Pemberton and Blackwood Valley, with about 24,400 acres of vines. In Great Southern, Geographe and Blackwood Valley, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon lead plantings.

australia/southern-fleurieu.text: A South Australian region in the Fleurieu area, on the Fleurieu Peninsula, which became an Australian Geographical Indication in 2001. It had about 1,300 acres planted as of 2014.

australia/southern-flinders-ranges.text: A region in the Far North of South Australia, the state that makes more than half of all Australian wine. It covers about 1,800 square miles but has only around 430 acres of vines.

australia/southern-highlands.text: A small New South Wales region in the South Coast zone, with about 350 acres of vines. Pinot Gris makes up more than half of plantings, with Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc next.

australia/southern-new-south-wales.text: A New South Wales zone containing Canberra District, Gundagai, Hilltops and Tumbarumba. Shiraz leads the plantings, then Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.

australia/strathbogie-ranges.text: A region in Central Victoria with about 1,300 acres of vines. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay lead plantings at roughly 30% and 27%, followed by Syrah.

australia/sunbury.text: A region northwest of Melbourne in the Port Phillip zone of Victoria, with vines going back to 1858 at Goona Warra and 1864 at Craiglee. Syrah makes up nearly half of plantings, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon.

australia/swan-district.text: A Western Australia region in Greater Perth, containing Swan Valley. Its plantings lean white, led by Verdelho and Chenin Blanc, then Chardonnay, with Syrah the top red.

australia/swan-hill.text: A region spanning the Murray River in Victoria and New South Wales, with almost all vineyards irrigated from the river. Irrigation began in the 1880s. The wines are known as fruit driven and suited to short to medium-term cellaring.

australia/swan-valley.text: A Western Australia subregion of Swan District in the upper reaches of the Swan River, registered in 2003.

australia/tasmania.text: Australia's southernmost wine state, with a cooler climate that can make distinctly different wines from the mainland. Pinot Noir is almost half of plantings, followed by Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc. Warming has helped grapes ripen fully.

australia/the-peninsulas.text: A very large zone of South Australia, the state that makes about half of all Australian wine. It covers about 12,300 square miles, but has only about 180 acres of vines, tiny compared with the area.

australia/tumbarumba.text: The coolest-climate grape-growing region in New South Wales, in the Southern New South Wales zone on the western foothills of the Snowy Mountains at 980 to 2,600 feet. It is known for sparkling wines and cool-climate table wines, with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir leading.

australia/upper-hunter-valley.text: A subregion in the Hunter region of the Hunter Valley zone in New South Wales, with about 1,200 acres of vines.

australia/upper-goulburn.text: A region in Central Victoria with about 720 acres of vines. Chardonnay leads plantings at 25%, followed by Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc.

australia/victoria.text: The Australian state with more wine producers than any other, though third in output. Syrah and Chardonnay are mainstays, and reds range from light, elegant Pinot Noir to full-bodied Shiraz. Rutherglen is known for its fortified Muscat.

australia/west-australian-south-east-coa.text: A very large Western Australia zone of about 67,000 square kilometers, listed directly under the country. It is a broad geographic label, not a single style of wine.

australia/western-australia.text: Australia's largest state, with wine regions almost entirely in the cooler south-western tip. It makes less than 5% of the country's wine but wins 30 percent of its medals.

australia/western-plains.text: A huge New South Wales zone of about 324,000 square kilometers. Plantings are led by Syrah, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Ruby Cabernet, all red.

australia/western-victoria.text: A Victorian zone from the South Australia border to Ballarat, containing the regions Grampians, Henty and Pyrenees. Pinot Noir leads plantings, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay and Syrah.

australia/wrattonbully.text: A region in the Limestone Coast zone of South Australia, with about 6,600 acres of vines. Cabernet Sauvignon makes up almost half of plantings, followed by Syrah at 28%.

australia/yarra-valley.text: A cool-climate region east of Melbourne in the Port Phillip zone of Victoria, best known for Chardonnay, sparkling wine and Pinot Noir. Pinot Noir is 40% of plantings. It draws many visitors thanks to its closeness to the city.

south-africa.text: Wine goes back to 1659 in Cape Town, and production sits almost entirely in the Western Cape. Chenin Blanc is the most planted grape, then Sauvignon Blanc, Colombard and Cabernet Sauvignon. About 60 Wine of Origin appellations are ranked as regions, districts and wards.

south-africa/agterkliphoogte.text: A ward in the Robertson area of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/bamboes-bay.text: A ward in the Olifants River area of the Western Cape.

south-africa/banghoek.text: A ward in the Stellenbosch area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/boesmansrivier.text: A ward in the Robertson area of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/bonnievale.text: A ward in the Robertson area of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/bot-river.text: A ward in the Walker Bay area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/bottelary.text: A ward in the Stellenbosch area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/breede-river-valley.text: A region of the Western Cape, with three districts: Breedekloof, Robertson and Worcester. Plantings in Robertson are led by Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Chenin Blanc.

south-africa/breedekloof.text: One of three districts in the Breede River Valley region, with 28 wine cellars and 14.24% of South Africa's vineyard plantings. Most traditional grapes grow here, and Chenin Blanc is the most planted.

south-africa/buffeljags.text: A ward in the Swellendam area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/calitzdorp.text: A district in the Klein Karoo area of the Western Cape.

south-africa/cape-agulhas.text: A district on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape, that contains the Elim ward.

south-africa/cape-peninsula.text: A district in the Coastal Region of the Western Cape.

south-africa/cape-south-coast.text: A region of the Western Cape, whose districts are Cape Agulhas, Elgin, Lower Duivenhoks River, Overberg, Plettenberg Bay, Swellendam and Walker Bay. Sauvignon Blanc is the most planted grape at 29%, followed by Chardonnay and Pinot Noir at 14% each.

south-africa/cederberg.text: A ward in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/ceres.text: A ward in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/citrusdal-mountain.text: A district in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape, with Piekenierskloof inside.

south-africa/citrusdal-valley.text: A district in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/coastal-region.text: A large region of the Western Cape containing Paarl, Stellenbosch, Swartland, Constantia and Franschhoek. Plantings across Paarl, Swartland and Stellenbosch are led by Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah.

south-africa/constantia.text: A ward in the Coastal Region, in the district of Constantia at Cape Town, known for a sweet wine made from Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains. It was exported widely to Europe in the 18th and 19th centuries, stopped after phylloxera, and resumed at Klein Constantia in 1986.

south-africa/darling.text: A district in the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape, with Groenekloof inside.

south-africa/devon-valley.text: A ward in the Stellenbosch area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/durbanville.text: A ward in the Tygerberg area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/eilandia.text: A ward in the Robertson district of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/elgin.text: A ward in the Overberg area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/elim.text: A ward in the Cape Agulhas area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/franschhoek-franschhoek-val.text: A district in the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/goudini.text: A ward in the Breedekloof district of the Breede River Valley, one of three districts in that region.

south-africa/greyton.text: A ward in the Overberg area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/groenekloof.text: A ward in the Darling area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/hemel-en-aarde-ridge.text: A ward in the Walker Bay area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/hemel-en-aarde-valley.text: A ward in the Walker Bay area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/herbertsdale.text: A ward on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/hoopsrivier.text: A ward in the Robertson district of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/hout-bay.text: A ward in the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/jonkershoek-valley.text: A ward in the Stellenbosch area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/klaasvoogds.text: A ward in the Robertson district of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/klein-karoo.text: A region of the Western Cape, containing Calitzdorp, Montagu, Tradouw and Outeniqua. Colombard is the most planted grape at 34%, followed by Chenin Blanc at 22%, with some Muscat of Alexandria.

south-africa/klein-rivier.text: A ward in the Overberg area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/koekenaap.text: A ward in the Lutzville Valley district of the Olifants River, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/lamberts-bay.text: A ward in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/langeberg-garcia.text: A district in the Klein Karoo area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/le-chasseur.text: A ward in the Robertson district of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/lutzville-valley.text: A district of the Coastal Region, on the lower Olifants River in the Western Cape, with Koekenaap inside.

south-africa/malgas.text: A ward in the Swellendam area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/malmesbury.text: A ward in the Swartland area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/mcgregor.text: A ward in the Robertson district of the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/montagu.text: A ward in the Klein Karoo area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/olifants-river.text: A region of the Western Cape, whose districts are Citrusdal Mountain and Citrusdal Valley, with the wards of Spruitdrift and Vredendal. Chenin Blanc (29%) and Colombard (26%) lead plantings, well ahead of Sauvignon Blanc and Pinotage.

south-africa/outeniqua.text: A ward in the Klein Karoo area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/overberg.text: A district on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape, with Elandskloof/Kaaimansgat, Greyton, Klein River and Theewater inside.

south-africa/paarl.text: A district in the Coastal Region of the Western Cape, whose wards are Agter-Paarl, Simonsberg-Paarl and Voor Paardeberg.

south-africa/papegaaiberg.text: A ward in the Stellenbosch area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/philadelphia.text: A ward in the Tygerberg area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/piekenierskloof.text: A ward in the Citrusdal Mountain district of the Olifants River, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/plettenberg-bay.text: A district on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/polkadraai-hills.text: A ward in the Stellenbosch area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/prince-albert-valley.text: A ward in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/riebeekberg.text: A ward in the Swartland area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/robertson.text: A district in the Breede River Valley, in the Western Cape, containing McGregor, Bonnievale, Le Chasseur and others. Plantings are spread across Colombard (14%), Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay (13% each) and Chenin Blanc.

south-africa/scherpenheuvel.text: A ward in the Breedekloof district of the Breede River Valley, one of three districts in that region.

south-africa/simonsberg-paarl.text: A ward in the Paarl area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/simonsberg-stellenbosch.text: A ward in the Stellenbosch area of the Coastal Region, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/slanghoek.text: A ward in the Breedekloof district of the Breede River Valley, one of three districts in that region.

south-africa/spruitdrift.text: A ward in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/stellenbosch.text: A district in the Coastal Region of the Western Cape, containing wards such as Banghoek, Bottelary, Devon Valley, Jonkershoek Valley and Simonsberg-Stellenbosch. Cabernet Sauvignon leads plantings at 20%, followed by Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot and Syrah.

south-africa/stilbaai-east.text: A ward on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/stormsvlei.text: A ward in the Swellendam area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/sunday-s-glen.text: A ward in the Walker Bay area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/swartberg.text: A ward in the Olifants River area, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/swartland.text: A district in the Coastal Region of the Western Cape, containing Malmesbury and Riebeekberg. Chenin Blanc leads plantings at 20%, followed by Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinotage.

south-africa/swellendam.text: A district on the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape, with Buffeljags, Malgas and Stormsvlei inside.

south-africa/theewater.text: A ward in the Overberg area of the Cape South Coast, in the Western Cape.

south-africa/tradouw.text: A ward in the Klein Karoo area, in the Western Cape.
